summary: Recovered the first-stage decoded payload from the custom XOR+add+byteswap decode loop (sub_401B84, 0x401B84). Live-tracing confirmed the entry gate passes to the loader chain (no __halt), the GlobalFlags anti-debug site returns 0x8000, and the decode loop transform (out=(src^key)+1; key=bswap(out), seed key 0x22CC456A, size 0x6BC). The debugger diverged into an anti-debug int3 hotpatch path on the disguised HeapCreate call ((char*)&HeapCreate-2 = 0x75970CDE). The decode is fully deterministic, so the payload was recovered analytically by reading the 1724-byte source at 0x401ED1 and re-implementing the loop: a 1728-byte x86 shellcode stub. The shellcode PEB-walks (fs:[0x30] at 0x1B6), hash-resolves APIs from Kernel32.dll and msvcrt.dll, scans for MZ/PE signatures, and allocates a RWX region (VirtualAlloc 0,0x6AC,0x1000,0x40). Artifact sha256 9f8e47944d294db5888d3cab9dd35f43f212b8b7dff92ae4439fe5358d7303e3. This is a stage-1 shellcode handoff, not a PE; the second static pass should treat it as position-independent x86 code.

findings.title: Entry gate passes to loader chain
findings.description: Live single-stepping through start() at 0x401510 confirmed the obfuscated gate computes ecx=(ror(*(dword*(NSPStartup PE header+0x1C)),8)) = 0xE6, then sub cl,0x50 = 0x96. The jb 0x401541 (__halt) branch is NOT taken; control falls through NOPs to jmp 0x401080 -> sub_40108C (loader chain).
findings.reasoning: At 0x401533 sub cl,ah with cl=0xE6, ah=0x50 yields 0x96 with no borrow, so CF=0 and jb is not taken. EIP advanced 0x401510->0x401515->...->0x40153C->0x401080->0x40108C exactly as static pass-1 predicted (bp-001 success).

evidence.observation: ecx=0xE6 after ror 8 at 0x40152E; sub cl,ah -> 0x96; jb not taken; jmp 0x401080 reached.

findings.title: Anti-debug GlobalFlags returns 0x8000
findings.description: At the first GlobalFlags call site (0x40104D, call dword ptr cs:[eax] with eax=0x403010 import slot), the resolved API returned 0x8000. The global heap flags under the x64dbg-managed heap are non-zero.
findings.reasoning: The import slot at 0x403010 held 0x75968560. Stepping over the call returned EAX=0x8000. This is a heap flag value consistent with a debugger-managed heap, matching the static anti-debug hypothesis. Execution nonetheless proceeded into sub_401B84, so the check did not block the payload path.

evidence.observation: [0x403010]=0x75968560; after call EAX=0x8000; EIP returned to 0x401050.

limitations: Exact API at 0x75968560 not symbol-resolved; 0x8000 value interpretation is heuristic.

findings.title: Decode loop transform confirmed live
findings.description: Disassembly of sub_401B84 loop (0x401BF6-0x401C0B) confirms: eax=key; xor eax,[edx]; add eax,1; mov [ebx],eax; key=bswap(eax); edx+=4, ebx+=4. Seed key 0x22CC456A (mov edi,0x22CC456A at 0x401BE1). Size 0x6BC (1724) bytes. Source base 0x401ED1 with a 2-byte pre-advance; first dword copied raw.
findings.reasoning: Live disassembly at 0x401BF6-0x401C0B exactly matches static pass-1 fin-004, with the corrected seed constant 0x22CC456A (static text mis-typed 0x22CC816A). This deterministic transform was used for analytic recovery.

evidence.observation: 0x401BF6 xor eax,[edx]; 0x401BF8 add eax,1; 0x401BFB mov [ebx],eax; 0x401C09 bswap edi; seed 0x22CC456A at 0x401BE1.

limitations: Static pass-1 seed constant typo (0x22CC816A vs live 0x22CC456A) resolved by live disassembly.

findings.title: Decoded payload is a PEB-walking API-resolution shellcode stub
findings.description: The 1728-byte decoded artifact (not a PE) is x86 position-independent shellcode. It embeds the wide string 'Kernel32.dll' (call+0x1F at 0x20, string at 0x23), PEB-walks via fs:[0x30] (0x1B6), scans for MZ (0x5C3) and PE (0x5E2) signatures, hash-resolves APIs (GetProcAddress/HeapAlloc/HeapFree/VirtualAlloc patterns at 0x66-0x98, msvcrt.dll at 0x533), and allocates a RWX buffer VirtualAlloc(0,0x6AC,0x1000,0x40) at 0x9A.
findings.reasoning: objdump -b binary -m i386 disassembles the artifact into coherent x86 instructions: call/GetPC prologue, PE structure offsets (0x3C, 0x50 subsystem check), PEB TEB offset 0x30, export table walks, and an RWX VirtualAlloc. This is the characteristic shape of a first-stage shellcode loader that will decode/load a second-stage module in memory.

sources.location: objdump -b binary -m i386 + manual hex map

evidence.observation: 0x20 e8 1a 00 00 00 call; 0x23 'Kernel32.dll' UTF-16LE; 0x1B6 64 a1 30 00 00 00 mov eax,fs:[0x30]; 0x5C3 66 ba 4d 5a mov dx,0x5A4D; 0x5E2 50 45 'PE'; 0x9A VirtualAlloc(0,0x6AC,0x1000,0x40).

limitations: No live execution of the shellcode performed (host-side safety); API-resolver targets inferred from surrounding code, not symbol names.
Second-stage payload/configuration not present in this 1728-byte stage.
